stops.text: 1. Navigate to https://apps.ankiweb.net/ and click *Download*
2. Select your correct OS version and click to begin the download
3. Click on the installer to begin the process
4. Click through the installer wizard
5. Hit Finish, and Launch *Anki*
5. Select your *language*, and confirm
1. Click the *Sync* button on the top action bar
2. Enter in your account details, if it is your first time using Anki, click *sign up*
3. Follow the online sign up flow, and validate your email with Anki
4. Return to Anki, and enter in your credentials (if the dialog disappeared, press sync again)
5. Press OK to verify your credentails. Anki will now try to sync!
6. To sync again in the future, (save your Anki or pull latest version) press *Sync* as needed
1. Select the *gear icon* on any deck
2. Select the *"Options"* tab
3. Verify which settings profile you are using (I use default and apply it to all my decks)
4. Change your new cards/day to 9999 and Maximum reviews/day to 9999 so that Anki does not hide cards from you!
5. Scroll down to find the *FSRS* heading, and enable it.
6. FSRS is now enabled, and Anki will learn from your review history. To train your AI model, return to this screen and hit Optimize Presets.
7. Confirm your changes, and hit save to return to Anki
1. Select the *gear icon* on any deck
2. Select the *"Options"* tab
3. Scroll down to the FSRS section
4. Select Optimize Current Presets
5. If you have existing reviews, your FSRS will retrain on your data. Hit Ok.
6. Save your new training data to apply changes
Go to Brightspace and find the lecture
Find the "Anki" module and click download
Once it finishes downloading, click on the file
You can also click on the file in your downloads folder
Anki will open it, and hit "import"
Next click "show" to select all the newly imported cards
Press CTRL or CMD + A to select all the cards
Right click, and select "Change Deck"
Select your deck, or click "Add" to create a new one
Close the browser to see your cards
1. Select the *gear icon* on the deck you want to rename
2. Select the *"Rename"* option
3. Enter in your new deck name
4. Click Ok
1. Select *'Add'* in the top bar
2. Change your note type to *'Cloze'* by selecting the type box (mine is currently set to Basic)
3. Make sure *'Cloze'* is selected and click *Choose*
4. Enter or paste the text you want to study
5. Highlight the word or phrase you want to hide
6. Click the *[...]* button or press *Ctrl+Shift+C* - this will be your first 'fill in the blank'
7. Repeat for additional cloze deletions as needed
8. Review the generated cloze fields in your text
9. Additionally, you can copy any images you want to show up once the answer is shown and add them to the 'Extras Field'
10. Click *Add* to create the card and return to the main screen
11. Select the deck that you just created the cards in (mine is called Default)
12. Study your cards
1. Select *'Add'* in the top bar
2. Change your note type to *'Image Occlusion'* by selecting the type box
3. Select Choose
4. Copy a diagram/picture to your clipboard
5. Return to Anki and click *'Paste Image from Clipboard'*
5. Return to Anki and click *'Paste Image from Clipboard'*
6. Make sure the *rectangle tool* is selected on the sidebar
8. Click and drag to draw rectangles over the information you are testing
9. Click and drag existing rectangles to resize/reposition them
10. Click *Add* and return to the main screen
11. Study your cards
If you want Anking cards from an Amboss question, click "Get Anki Cards"
Review the suggested cards, and uncheck if not needed - then click "Copy Anki query"
Navigate back to Anki and hit Browse
Paste the copied query into the search bar, and press enter
Review the cards, and select the ones you want to unsuspend (I selected all with CTRL + A)
Right click, and select "Toggle Suspend"
Close the browser, and now your cards are ready to study
After finding a question you want Anking cards for, find the "Question id:" box
Select and copy the question Id (ex: 3110)
Return back to Anki, and hit *Browse*
Inside the search bar, type in tag:\*UWorld\*: followed by the question id, ex: tag:\*UWorld\*:3110
Press enter and review the matched cards
Select the cards (CTRL + A to select All), and right click
Select "Toggle Suspend"
Close the Browser to review the cards
